100 simulated perspectives.
A stronger game.

My assessment: keep the simple, game-first approach. Strengthen unfamiliar cases and the evidence behind a completion.

This is an AI-simulated review. The 100 profiles are constructed evaluation perspectives, not recruited people. Source inspection, scripted checks and selected browser interactions support the software findings. No human satisfaction scores, completion rates, learning gains or training-efficiency results were measured.

Preserve the approachable beginning.

The early games make useful distinctions visible through action. Later challenges need to test whether the player can recognize the principle when the answer is less clearly signposted. These judgments are design assessments to test with actual learners.

Scheduling

A concrete plan

Selection, priority, unavailable resources, work timing, curing and changing a checkerboard all produce observable decisions.

Next: Later challenges should require a short justification of trade-offs and test unfamiliar constraints.

Analysis

Build the answer

The player constructs rates, balances stacks, compares spread, traces trends and keeps reports in scope.

Next: The final report should eventually combine more analytical skills and require choosing an appropriate method.

Documentation

Trace the work

Applicability, approved revisions, forecasts, prerequisites and completion evidence are modeled separately.

Next: The final pack still supplies strong cues. Add a later case that requires discovering the right requirement.

Database Management

Keep the service usable

Access, unique identity, dependencies, safe changes and recovery form a progressive path.

Next: Later troubleshooting should require interpreting symptoms; recovery should verify record contents as well as counts.

Data Integrity

Trust the record

Unknown versus zero, units, duplicate identity, reconciliation and correction history are handled explicitly.

Next: Later repair should require choosing keep, correct, hold or investigate and selecting supporting evidence.

Can someone independently do the work?

The current game gives evidence of selections, calculations and modeled decisions. It provides less evidence of discovering an unfamiliar requirement, explaining a trade-off, or defending a conclusion.

DiscoverEvaluateDecideActCommunicateDefend

Keep the small early wins. Add a later combined shift where a change affects the plan, the records and the report. Ask the player to select supporting evidence and briefly explain the consequential decision.

Concrete findings led to concrete fixes.

The changes below are implemented in the updated game. Existing unfinished Analysis and Database Management cases retain their original facts; newly generated cases use the expanded scenarios.

✓

Vary the real task

Analysis pooling and report cases now use unequal groups with totals beyond 100. New cases require finding the denominator.

✓

Let a neutral pattern be correct

Trend cases can be level. Scatter cases can support No linear trend without claiming that no relationship exists.

✓

Remove a keyboard answer shortcut

Documentation moves focus to the next stage tab. It no longer focuses the next correct answer automatically.

✓

Keep keyboard players in place

Failed checks retain focus on the Check control instead of returning the player to the top-level page.

✓

Show which records were reviewed

Data Integrity keeps a Reviewed marker even when the original record was already correct.

✓

Distinguish an example from completion

Viewed demonstrations get their own marker and no longer increase the completed-level count.

✓

Make identity matching matter

The account cards no longer disclose which same-name account is approved. The player must match the unique identifier.

✓

Vary the combined service challenge

Database Management changes access tasks, scopes, excess/missing keys and failed dependencies across new cases.

Explore all 100 perspectives.

20 per specialty: five experience groups × four play contexts. Each profile emphasizes one specialty. Together the review covers all five paths and four worlds. These reactions are hypotheses, not quotations or votes from real people. Concerns describe the reviewed baseline; the findings section identifies fixes.

What was actually checked.

All 55 level models were exercised through deterministic tests. Additional checks covered saved progress, case revisions, demonstration status and interaction regressions. Browser checks reproduced the lost keyboard focus and verified the repaired focus path and reviewed-record marker. These are software checks, not tests of learning effectiveness.

  • Scheduling32,052 assertions passed
  • Analysis6,670 assertions passed
  • Documentation6,040 assertions passed
  • Database Management4,301 assertions passed
  • Data Integrity2,021 assertions passed
  • Navigation and saved cases225 assertions passed

The browser checks are representative, not 100 human play sessions. Native phone usability, motivation, retention and real-work transfer remain unmeasured.

Use real learners for the next evidence.

A proposed working-group pilot can stay simple. Observe actual decisions and work products, then compare like-for-like tasks. Do not turn a simulated panel into an approval vote.

1 · Establish the starting point

Give a short unfamiliar task before play. Record accuracy, constraints missed, explanation quality, assistance and time. Include both newcomers and experienced personnel.

2 · Observe the game

Let participants play without coaching every click. Note where they pause, guess, seek hints, switch specialties or misread an instruction. Collect their own words.

3 · Test transfer

Use a different case after play, with changed facts and fewer cues. Require a usable work product and a short evidence-based explanation. Include a later retention check.

4 · Compare and calibrate

Have two evaluators independently use the same rubric. Check where their judgments disagree. Add a comparable conventional-training group before making efficiency claims.

Four-hour proficiency and tenfold efficiency remain research goals. Game stars are practice feedback. The source review covers the main game; the earlier practice workspace is a separate experience.
